extracted.intended_audience: agency rulemakers, agency counsel, administrative law practitioners, hearing officers
extracted.subtask_description: Illustrative procedural rules for agency adjudications covering service of process, subpoenas, depositions/interrogatories, and official notice — intended as a model rule set for agencies implementing APA-related hearings and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative rule on service of papers: (i) By Whom Served — 'The Agency shall serve all orders, notices and other papers issued by it... Every other paper shall be served by the party filing it.' (ii) Upon Whom Served — 'All papers served by either the Agency or any party shall be served upon all counsel of record ... and upon parties not represented by counsel or upon their agents designated by them or by law.' (iii) Service Upon Parties — 'The final order, and any paper required to be served by the Agency upon a party, shall be served upon such party or upon the agent designated by him or by law to receive service of such papers, and a copy shall be furnished to counsel of record.' (iv) Method of Service — 'Service of papers shall be mail, personally or, unless prohibited by law, by first-class or registered mail, telegraph or by publication.' (v) When Service Complete — 'Service upon parties shall be regarded as complete: by mail, upon deposit in the United States mail properly stamped and addressed; by telegraph, when deposited with a telegraph company properly addressed and with charges prepaid; by publication when due notice shall have been given ... as provided by law or rule.' (vi) Filing with Agency — 'Papers required to be filed with the Agency shall be deemed filed upon actual receipt by the Agency ... accompanied by proof of service ... Upon such actual receipt the filing shall be deemed complete as of the date of deposit in the mail or with the telegraph company.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies allocation of service responsibilities (agency vs. filing party), who must receive service (counsel of record and unrepresented parties/agents), permissible methods (personal service, mail, telegraph, publication unless prohibited), the moment service is complete (mail deposit/telegraph deposit/publication complying with law), and the rule that filings are 'deemed filed' on actual receipt but date-stamped to date of deposit. Includes requirement that counsel subsequently entering appearance notify others. Use these rules as a model; agencies may have statutory or regulatory variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoenas (form, issuance, service, fees, proof, quashing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative subpoena rule: (i) Form — 'Every subpena shall state the name of the Agency and the title of the proceeding ... and shall command the person ... to attend and give testimony or produce designated evidence at a specified time and place.' (ii) Issuance to Parties — 'Upon application of counsel (or other representative authorized to practice before the Agency) for any party ... there shall be issued to such party subpoenas requiring the attendance and testimony of witnesses or the production of evidence ... The agency may issue subpoenas to parties not so represented upon request or upon a showing of general relevance and reasonable scope.' (iii) Service — unless acknowledged, 'it shall be served by a person who is not a party and is not less than 18 years of age' by delivering a copy and tendering fees for one day's attendance and mileage; when issued on behalf of the United States, fees/mileage may but need not be tendered and service may be by registered mail. (iv) Fees — 'Witnesses summoned before an agency shall be paid ... the same fees and mileage that are paid to witnesses in the courts of the United States.' (v) Proof of Service — 'The person serving the subpena shall make proof of service by filing the subpena and the required return, affidavit, or acknowledgment of service ... Failure to make proof of service does not affect the validity of the service.' (vi) Quashing — 'Upon motion made promptly ... the Agency ... may (1) quash or modify the subpena if it is unreasonable or requires evidence not relevant to any matter in issue, or (2) condition denial of the motion upon just and reasonable conditions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes content and formalities of subpoenas, who may obtain them, service mechanics and who may serve, payment of witness fees, and proof-of-service requirements. Provides a protective mechanism (motion to quash or modify) where subpoenas are unreasonable or seek irrelevant evidence; agencies may impose reasonable conditions when denying quash motions. Note that failure to file proof does not invalidate service. When subpoenas are issued on behalf of the U.S., different service/fee practices may apply (registered mail acceptable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoenas — power to issue, geographic scope, enforcement, penalties (legislative provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions of the uniform subpoena rule that would require legislation: (viii) Power to Issue — '...such Agency or any member of such Agency, any hearing officer appointed pursuant to Section 11 ... or any officer designated by it may issue subpoenas requiring the attendance of witnesses to testify or to produce evidence.' (ix) Geographical Scope — 'Such attendance of witnesses and such production of evidence may be required from any place in the United States or any Territory or possession thereof, at any designated place of hearing.' (x) Enforcement — 'In case of contumacy or refusal to obey a subpoena ... any court of the United States ... upon application by the Agency, may issue an order requiring such person to appear ... and give testimony, or produce evidence.' (xi) Penalties — 'Any person who shall wilfully neglect or refuse to attend and testify or to produce evidence ... shall be guilty of an offense and upon conviction ... shall be punished by a fine of not more than $1,000 or by imprisonment for not more than one year, or by both.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recommended statutory authorities: explicit issuance power for agencies/hearing officers, nationwide geographic reach of subpoenas, judicial enforcement procedure (courts issuing orders to compel compliance), and criminal penalties for willful refusal. Agencies need enabling legislation to secure enforcement and penalty mechanisms described here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions — general procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative deposition rule provisions: Right to Take — 'any party may take the testimony of any person ... by deposition upon oral examination or written interrogatories for use as evidence in the proceeding' subject to exceptions. Scope — 'the deponent may be examined regarding any matter not privileged, which is relevant to the subject matter involved in the proceeding.' Officer Before Whom Taken — depositions within the United States before an officer authorized to administer oaths; in foreign countries before specified U.S. diplomatic/consular officers or a person designated by the Agency. Authorization/Notice — 'party desiring to take the deposition ... shall give reasonable notice in writing to the Agency and all parties' including time, place, and names (or descriptive class). Protection of Parties and Deponents — Agency may order limitations (place, written interrogatories only, exclude certain matters, limit scope, closed proceedings, sealing, protection of business secrets, simultaneous sealed filings, etc.) and may stop examinations for bad faith or undue annoyance. Oral Examination and Cross Examination — 'shall proceed as provided in rules governing the reception of evidence at an oral hearing'; written cross-interrogatories permitted. Recordation — officer shall put witness on oath and record testimony (typewriter/stenographic) and note objections on the deposition; objections not made at the time are waived. Signing, Attestation and Return — deposition transcribed submitted to witness for reading/signing (or officer states reason for refusal), officer certifies and sends sealed deposition to Agency Secretary; copies furnished on payment. Use and Effect — 'a deposition taken and filed ... will not become a part of the record ... until received in evidence by the hearing officer'; 'Except by agreement or ruling ... a deposition will be received only in its entirety.' Fees — deponents and officers entitled to same fees as in District Courts, paid by the party at whose instance the depositions are taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets comprehensive rules for taking depositions for agency proceedings: relevance and privilege limits, qualified officers to take oaths (domestic and foreign), required notice content and timing, protective orders for confidentiality/business secrets or to limit burdensome examinations, strictures on objections (must be made contemporaneously), attestation/filing procedures (sealed return to Agency Secretary), conditional use in the record (must be offered/received to become part of record), and fee/payment responsibilities. Emphasizes agency authority to tailor protections and to suspend/limit depositions for cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions upon Interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures where depositions are taken upon written interrogatories: Submission — 'the party offering the testimony shall separately and consecutively number each interrogatory and file and serve them with a notice stating the name and address of the person who is to answer them and the name or descriptive title and address of the officer before whom they are to be taken.' Timing — 'Within 10 days thereafter a party so served may serve cross-interrogatories ... Within five days thereafter, the latter may serve redirect interrogatories.' Interrogation process — officer reads interrogatories seriatim, records each question and answer with only the deponent, officer, and court reporter present. Attestation and Return — officer certifies under official signature and seal that deponent was duly sworn, that the interrogatories and answers are a true record, that only specified persons were present, and that officer/stenographer are not parties or interested; officer then sends original to Agency Secretary, a copy to counsel submitting the interrogatories and another to the deponent. 'In all other respects, depositions upon interrogatories shall be governed by the previous Deposition Rule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies form and sequential numbering of interrogatories, timelines for cross- and redirect interrogatories, presence restrictions during oral reading, officer attestation requirements, and return/filing channels. Treat these depositions largely like oral depositions for procedural protections, including the filing/attestation and use rules of the general deposition provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Notice (matters of law and material facts; procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative Official Notice rules: RULE 1 — MATTERS OF LAW: 'The Agency or its hearing officer, with or without prior request or notice, will officially notice: (i) Federal Law ... (ii) State Law ... (iii) Governmental Organization ... (iv) Agency Organization.' RULE 2 — MATERIAL FACTS: 'In the absence of controverting evidence, the Agency and its hearing officers, with or without prior notice or request may officially notice: (i) Agency Proceedings ... (ii) Business Customs ... (iii) Notorious Facts ... (iv) Technical Knowledge.' Conditions — Request or Suggestion: 'Any party may request, or the hearing officer or the agency may suggest, that official notice be taken of a material fact, which shall be clearly and precisely stated, orally on the record ... or by written notice ... at any time prior to a final decision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes lawful subjects appropriate for official notice (codified law, decisions, organizational facts) from material facts that can be noticed in absence of contrary evidence (agency records, business customs, notorious facts, technical knowledge within agency expertise). Provides procedure for parties to request official notice (clear, precise statement, oral or written, before final decision). Agencies should ensure notice is limited when controverted and provide parties opportunity to rebut or supply contrary evidence.
